## project:fieldops — Field operations platform · Professional work at Magenta Connect · 2025
Summary: One platform for field sales teams: dynamic forms, live tracking, and access that follows the org chart.
Problem: Field teams reported on paper, managers had no live view of the field, and every tier of the organization needed different access to the same data.
Approach: A schema-driven form engine non-technical admins can configure, hierarchical RBAC with action-level permissions, follow-up workflows with automated WhatsApp ledger sharing, and Google Maps tracking on refactored FastAPI services.
Result: Sales reporting went fully digital, managers see field operations as they happen, and the whole suite shares one centrally themed interface.
Stack: React, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Google Maps, RBAC

## project:analytics — AI analytics platform · Independent project
Summary: Instagram analytics you can talk to. Ask a question, get the trend and a strategy behind it.
Problem: Engagement metrics are only useful when people can find the story in them. The original university dashboard showed numbers but could not explain them.
Approach: Re-engineered the dashboard into a SaaS platform with Module Federation, so the analytics engine deploys on its own. An LLM agent uses retrieval over a vector database to answer questions about the data.
Result: Cross-profile dashboards for engagement, reach, and sentiment, plus natural-language questions that turn into marketing strategies.
Stack: Next.js, Module Federation, LLMs, RAG, Vector DB

## project:yashos — YashOS · Personal experiment, you are here · 2026
Summary: This portfolio. A tiny operating system with two personalities and a physics engine.
Problem: A portfolio can show how its maker thinks about interaction and detail, not just list a stack.
Approach: A window manager, a store built from small slices, and app interiors that each borrow a real app's shape. Every interaction honours reduced motion.
Result: The thing you are using right now. Try zero gravity from the menu bar.
Stack: Next.js, TypeScript, Zustand, Motion

## project:assistant — This assistant
Related: YashOS (project:yashos), LLMs (skill:llms), TypeScript (skill:typescript)
An AI assistant that Yash designed and built to answer visitors' questions about Yash's work, by text or by voice. It is made to live inside YashOS, Yash's portfolio site.

What it does: it answers only from a fixed knowledge base of Yash's roles, projects, skills and education, synced from YashOS, plus notes Yash writes. Every answer records which parts of that knowledge it used. When a question goes beyond the knowledge, it first gives the closest real evidence from Yash's work. If the visitor presses the same point, it says that isn't in what it knows rather than guessing, and points the visitor to Yash through Messages.

How it works, in plain words:
- One Cloudflare Worker serves it.
- Each conversation gets its own Durable Object, a small stateful server process that holds that conversation's history and runs the voice loop on the server.
- The language model and the voice come from MiniMax. Text answers come from MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, the only candidate that passed the assistant's safety test; the model for voice is still being chosen by measured speed.
- The whole knowledge base sits at the front of the prompt instead of being searched piece by piece, so the model sees all of it at once and the provider can cache it.
- In voice mode, Deepgram Flux on Cloudflare Workers AI turns speech into text and decides when the visitor has finished speaking. MiniMax then speaks the reply one sentence at a time, so the voice can start before the whole reply is written.
- The model, speech-to-text and voice providers each sit behind a small interface with a scripted stand-in, so the tests and a demo mode run without any API keys.
- An eval suite of about 40 test questions runs against the real model. It checks that the assistant sticks to the knowledge, offers the closest evidence without implying a yes, corrects false premises and ignores instructions pasted into a message. Every answer also passes an output check before it is shown or spoken, and a grounding check that every name and number appears in the knowledge it cited.

The design document and the source code are public, including the assistant's instructions and this knowledge base.
